Subject: Instant-on SLO runbook and demo — post-call recap

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Short post-call recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the SLO gating for your payments API use case. I focused this on the "instant-on" path we discussed (sub-100ms token latency for small inference calls, steady-state throughput at ~1.2k reqs/sec across bursts).

Key notes from discovery:
- Primary SLO target: P95 response <= 120ms for synchronous 0.5–2 token prompts (your gateway will batch minimal metadata).
- Throughput expectation: sustained 700–1,200 rps, with amplitude bursts up to 6k rps for 90s during marketing events.
- Concurrency profile: typical steady concurrency ~90 vCPU-equivalent sessions; bursts push concurrent active streams to ~800 for short windows.
- Streaming: you require token-level streaming for early confirmation to the client (WebSocket), with tail latency <= 250ms under burst.
- Safety nets: queueing with prioritized fast-path for authenticated high-priority traffic; fallback to smaller model variant when warm pool exhausted.

Open items we agreed to action:
1) Rishi / Marissa: produce a one-page SLO matrix (P50/P90/P95/P99) + warm pool sizing scenarios (attached draft).
2) QuickPay: share one representative traffic trace (5–10 minutes) with masked payloads so we can validate sequence length distribution and burst shape.
3) Ops exercise: run a short simulated marketing-burst demo (30–90s, 2x expected peak) — target week of Nov 13th.
4) Contract note: Ben to follow up on reserved capacity pricing once we converge on warm pool size.

Immediate ask from you: please confirm (a) whether 120ms P95 is acceptable as an initial gating SLO, and (b) availability for the ops demo week of Nov 13–17.

Attachments: slo-matrix-v0.3.xlsx (draft), warmup-capacity-scenarios.pdf (examples).

Best,
Rishi
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Elena — thanks. A few technical clarifications and the updated mini-runbook (summary below). Marissa attached a brief appendix with warm-pool sizing rationale.

Quick answers:
- Warm pool reclaim: warm slots can be evicted and returned to the shared pool in ~18–45s depending on model and kv-cache size; for the smallest transformer we saw ~18s median reclaim, larger models push toward the 40s range.
- Priority lane: yes — we can mark up to 7% of warm pool as "priority" so those requests skip the normal queue. That is enforced by token-level policy and per-customer tokens.

Proposed minimal runbook (automated path):
1) Monitor P95 rolling 2-min window.
2) If P95 > 160ms for 60s: scale warm pool +20% if capacity available.
3) If P95 > 200ms for 2 mins: trigger auto-fallback to the small model variant; send urgent alert to ops + customer success.
4) If queue depth > 300 and scaling did not restore P95 within 90s: enable shedding for low-priority traffic and increase priority-lane reserve to 12% (manual approval required thereafter).

Next steps we will take this week:
- Marissa: final SLO matrix + warm-pool scenarios (v0.4).
- Ben: initial reserved capacity pricing estimate (commit tiers: 6m / 12m).
- Rishi: finalize ops demo agenda and send calendar invite for Nov 13 morning PT.

Tom / Elena — does the automation path above match your risk tolerance? If so we'll bake it into the demo and the SLO matrix.

Thanks,
Rishi

- Two warm-pool options: "lean" (targets 1.2k sustained, 3.5k burst, median reclaim 40s) and "aggressive" (targets 2k sustained, 6k burst, median reclaim 18s).
- Recommended emergency reserve: 7% priority-lane; can be raised to 12% under manual escalation.
